meta_description: Free, fully offline OpenStreetMap maps for the Kiwix reader. Vector tiles, satellite imagery, 3D terrain, and Wikipedia info — works without an internet connection on iOS, Android, Mac, Windows, and Linux.
tagline: Fully offline OpenStreetMap maps for the Kiwix reader. Vector tiles, satellite imagery, 3D terrain, and Wikipedia — no internet connection required.
badge_mac_title: Kiwix on the Mac App Store
maps_intro: Pick a region below, install Kiwix, and open the .zim file. Hosted on the Internet Archive — each download includes a torrent.
maps_intro_lang: Pick a region below and download it in English: its map labels, search and Wikipedia are in English. Open the file in Kiwix, a free app; each map's page shows how, step by step.
feature_key_intro: Badges on each card show what's inside:
badge_photo_desc: find a place from a photo of a sign.
what_lead: StreetZim packages OpenStreetMap data — entire countries or continents — into a single ZIM file you can open in Kiwix. It works completely offline: no servers, no API calls, no internet required after the initial download.
what_p2: Unlike traditional offline map apps that ship raster tiles, StreetZim uses vector tiles rendered client-side with MapLibre GL JS. The result: smooth pan, zoom, rotation, and even 3D terrain — all from a single file on your device.
feat_vector_p: Smooth, sharp street-level maps with the OpenMapTiles schema, rendered live by MapLibre.
feat_sat_p: 10-meter resolution Sentinel-2 cloudless imagery for the entire mapped region.
feat_terrain_p: Hillshade and 3D elevation from the Copernicus GLO-30 global DEM.
feat_wiki_p: Tap any city, mountain, or landmark for its Wikipedia article and key facts.
feat_search_p: Search across millions of place names, streets, parks, peaks, airports, and POIs.
feat_offline_p: Just one .zim file. No accounts, no telemetry, no network. Open and go.
step1_p: Free reader for iOS, Android, Mac, Windows, and Linux. Get it at kiwix.org. On Windows and Linux, open maps in the Kiwix PWA for now: Kiwix Desktop 2.5 shows them blank, and its fix is only in the nightly builds so far.
step2_p: Pick a region above and download the .zim file (or grab the torrent for faster speeds).
step2_p_lang: Pick a region above and press its download button: you get the map in English, as one .zim file.
step3_p: Open the .zim file in the Kiwix app. That’s it — the map runs entirely offline.
sources_intro: StreetZim is built entirely from open data. Each map ZIM bundles content from these sources:
src_map: Map data: © OpenStreetMap contributors, available under the Open Database License (ODbL).
src_sat: Satellite imagery: EOxCloudless https://cloudless.eox.at by EOX IT Services GmbH (Contains modified Copernicus Sentinel data 2021) — CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, non-commercial use only.
src_elev: Elevation: Copernicus GLO-30 DEM — © DLR / Airbus, provided under the COPERNICUS programme by the European Union and ESA.
src_place: Place info: Wikidata (CC0) and Wikipedia (CC BY-SA 3.0).

kg_h2: How to open the map in Kiwix
kg_android_1: Install Kiwix from Google Play. It is free.
kg_android_2: Download the map above. Your phone saves it in Downloads.
kg_android_3: Open Kiwix, go to its library and add the file you downloaded.
kg_ios_1: Install Kiwix from the App Store. It is free.
kg_ios_2: Download the map above. Safari saves it in the Files app, under Downloads.
kg_ios_3: Open Kiwix, go to its library and open the file from Downloads.
kg_mac_1: Install Kiwix from the Mac App Store, then open the downloaded file with it.
kg_pc_1: Open the Kiwix web app in your browser and choose the downloaded file. Kiwix Desktop 2.5 shows these maps blank; its fix is only in the nightly builds so far.
kg_offline: After that, the map works without an internet connection.
